currentObjective: Harden bounded direct-recursion recurrence behavior through characterization, documentation, and package validation
completedStep: 10/11 — characterization, performance, docs and package hardening
decisions: Phase 6 starts from Phase 5 cycle boundaries and may solve only supported direct recursion with sufficient base-case evidence.
Recurrence extraction and recurrence solving remain separate responsibilities.
The recurrence model is internal to the analyzer and independent from ComplexityExpression and inherited solver projects.
Recursive calls must be counted per execution path, so mutually exclusive branches do not add multiplicity while sequential calls on the same path may.
Supported initial reductions are constant positive decrements and constant scale reductions proven from syntax and semantics.
Unsupported, invalid, unsafe, numerically inconclusive, and mutually recursive patterns remain Unknown.
RecurrenceRelation stores ComplexityVariable, immutable recursive terms, and NonRecursiveWork as ComplexityExpression without Roslyn syntax or symbols.
RecurrenceTerm stores integer positive Multiplicity and a RecurrenceReduction with either SubtractConstant c > 0 or Scale q where 0 < q < 1.
RecurrenceSolution is a future solver outcome value with Solved, Unsupported, Invalid, and NumericallyInconclusive states; no solver is implemented in step 2.
PolynomialLogComplexity now stores normalized double polynomial degrees so fractional powers such as O(n^1.585) share the existing polylog model.
Polynomial exponents normalize near integers within 1e-9 and format non-integers with three deterministic decimal places, trimming trailing zeros with invariant culture.
RecursiveCallAnalyzer identifies only semantically direct recursive invocations with SymbolEqualityComparer.Default and keeps same-name overloads out of direct recursion.
Recursive call shapes store per-eligible-parameter argument relations, preserving the correct input-size variable instead of assuming the first parameter.
Recursive argument reduction extraction recognizes positive constant decrements and constant scale reductions, including n - c, n + (-c), n / b, n * q, and q * n where supported.
Recursive execution paths distinguish sequential recursive calls from mutually exclusive branch alternatives, so binary-search-style branches produce one recursive call per path.
Base-case evidence extraction is conservative and recognizes simple terminating if branches guarded by bounded comparisons such as n <= constant or n == constant.
SummationRecurrenceSolver solves only T(n)=T(n-c)+f(n) with one multiplicity-one constant-decrement term and supported polylog local work.
For supported summation recurrences, the solver increments the polynomial degree by one and preserves the log exponent; c does not affect the Big-O class.
SummationRecurrenceSolver returns structured Invalid or Unsupported outcomes instead of converting unsupported shapes to a hidden null or known complexity.
ConstantCoefficientRecurrenceSolver solves only same-decrement multiplicity aT(n-c)+polylog with a > 1 and the positive second-order subset a1T(n-1)+a2T(n-2)+polylog where a1 >= 0 and a2 > 0.

Same-decrement multiplicity uses the homogeneous exponential base a^(1/c), and positive second-order solving uses the bounded quadratic formula for r^2 = a1*r + a2 without MathNet, matrices, or a general root solver.
Exponential bases now normalize deterministically using invariant culture, integer tolerance, and three fractional decimal places, so Fibonacci-like results format as O(1.618^n).
MasterTheoremRecurrenceSolver solves only one normalized scale term aT(qn)+supported polylog local work, with a >= 1, 0 < q < 1, and b = 1/q > 1.
Master Theorem critical exponent p is computed with System.Math.Log(a) / System.Math.Log(b), normalized through PolynomialExponentNormalizer, and formatted with the deterministic real-power policy.

Master Theorem case selection uses centralized RecurrenceNumerics tolerances: polynomial gap threshold for cases 1 and 3, comparison epsilon for case 2, and NumericallyInconclusive for the unsupported boundary gap.
Case 3 is returned only for supported polylog tolls whose equivalent regularity ratio a*q^k is strictly below one; unsupported local work and unsupported recurrence shapes remain Unsupported.
